title: The Cell and Molecular Pathology of Tau Protein in Alzheimer’s Disease
content: In the brain of Alzheimer´s disease (AD) patients, tau protein abnormally aggregates into pathologic paired helical filaments (PHFs), which massively coalesces into neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs). These structures are responsible for most cell death reported in this neuropathological disorder. Aggregation of Tau is produced when the molecule abnormally undergoes several posttranslational modifications, such as abnormal phosphorylation, conformational changes, and truncation [1]. However, the order and timing in which Tau modifications occur and progress during the formation and proliferation of NFTS are still under profound investigation. To get more insights into deciphering the contribution of these modifications of Tau on the genesis and maturation of NFTs, we have analyzed the brains of human subjects who developed AD with variable levels of clinical manifestation of cognitive decline. Brain sections from the hippocampus of AD cases were processed for multiple immunofluorescence labeling using antibodies to distinct modifications of tau protein, such as phosphorylation, truncation, ubiquitination, and conformational changes. Morphological analysis of the patterns of staining and colocalization was performed using confocal microscopy.
